titre: The Bill That Replaced a Declaration of War
accroche: In 1872 in Geneva, five judges order Great Britain to pay $15.5 million in gold. The United States gives up on war.
contenu_vulgarise:
During the American Civil War, a shipyard in Birkenhead, England, builds a cruiser for the Confederate navy, christened the CSS Alabama. The ship, armed and equipped while Great Britain officially declares itself neutral, captures or sinks more than sixty Northern merchant ships before being sunk in turn off the French coast, in June 1864, by the USS Kearsarge. At the end of the war, in 1865, Washington demands reparation from London for the damage caused by the Alabama and by ships built under the same conditions.

## A tribunal instead of a fleet

For six years, the claim poisons relations between the two countries: some in Washington raise the possibility of demanding British Canada as compensation. A break is avoided by a choice that was unusual for the time. On May 8, 1871, the two governments sign the Treaty of Washington, in which Great Britain expresses regret for the escape of the Alabama and similar cruisers, without admitting fault. The U.S. Senate ratifies it on May 24. The treaty submits the dispute to an arbitral tribunal of five members, appointed respectively by the United Kingdom, the United States, Italy, Switzerland and Brazil, and sets out three rules of due diligence that a neutral state must observe to prevent its territory from being used to equip a belligerent's ships, rules that international law did not yet know in so precise a form.

The tribunal sits in Geneva, at the Hôtel de Ville (City Hall), beginning on December 15, 1871. It dismisses from the outset the so-called indirect claims, those concerning the supposed prolongation of the war itself, and retains only the material damage directly caused by the cruisers. On September 14, 1872, it orders Great Britain to pay $15.5 million in gold to the United States as compensation for that damage alone.

## What arbitration replaces

The case is often presented as the moment when two powers capable of going to war with each other choose to replace it with a judgment expressed in a figure, enforceable, and accepted in advance by both parties. Great Britain pays without having admitted fault, and both countries give up any later claim tied to the same conflict: the sum closes the dispute rather than merely documenting it. This mechanism, a neutral third party who settles by a figure rather than a victor who imposes his will, is what the twentieth century would generalize under the name of international arbitration.

repere.texte: The Geneva tribunal orders Great Britain to pay $15,500,000 in gold to the United States, as compensation for the damage caused by a ship that had alone captured more than sixty merchant ships.
repere.source: Arbitral award of September 14, 1872, Alabama claims of the United States of America against Great Britain, Reports of International Arbitral Awards, vol. XXIX

carte.punch: Two countries capable of going to war choose a figure instead of a battle.
carte.idee: In 1872, a neutral tribunal meeting in Geneva judges the dispute arising from Confederate warships built in England during the American Civil War. It orders Great Britain to pay $15.5 million in gold to the United States, which in exchange gives up any further claim.

quiz.question: What does the 1871 Treaty of Washington change compared with the usual way of settling a dispute between two great powers in the nineteenth century?
choix: It transfers the dispute to an already existing permanent international organization
It requires the losing party to publicly acknowledge its responsibility
It sets the amount of reparation in advance, before any judgment
It entrusts the decision to a neutral tribunal whose judgment binds both parties in advance
quiz.explication: The treaty does not merely name an arbitrator: both governments commit in advance to accept the Geneva tribunal's judgment, whatever it may be. That is what distinguishes arbitration from simple mediation, and what allows Great Britain to pay without admitting fault, or losing face.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What does the CSS Alabama do before being sunk off the French coast in June 1864?
choix: It bombards the port of Boston twice
It carries weapons intended for the British army in India
It captures or sinks more than sixty Northern merchant ships
It serves as the flagship of the Confederate fleet for two years
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The body of the entry states that the Alabama captures or sinks more than sixty Northern merchant ships before being sunk by the USS Kearsarge in June 1864.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What does the Treaty of Washington of May 8, 1871 set out, in addition to submitting the dispute to an arbitral tribunal?
choix: The exact amount of the compensation the losing party will have to pay
The obligation for Great Britain to publicly acknowledge its fault
The future composition of the government of the Confederate States
Three rules of due diligence that a neutral state must observe toward belligerents
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The treaty sets out three rules of due diligence that a neutral state must observe to prevent its territory from being used to equip a belligerent's ships.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Which claims does the Geneva tribunal dismiss from the outset, in 1871?
choix: Claims concerning ships built after the end of the war
Indirect claims, concerning the supposed prolongation of the war itself
Claims brought by private individuals rather than by the American state
Claims based on ships other than the CSS Alabama
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The tribunal dismisses from the outset the so-called indirect claims, those concerning the supposed prolongation of the war itself, and retains only the direct damage.
